name: Fuligni Brunello di Montalcino 2018
text:
## Fuligni Brunello di Montalcino 2018

**The story.** Fuligni, in [Montalcino](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Fuligni,+Montalcino,+Italy&t=k), has been led since 1971 by Maria Flora Fuligni, with her long-time right hand, Dr Daniela Perino, now the estate's CEO; Decanter calls it "one of the denomination's most consistent performers" ([Nicks Wine Merchants, critics' notes](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2018-fuligni-brunello-di-montalcino)).

**Brunello in brief.** "Brunello", from *bruno*, brown, was the local name for what was thought to be a separate grape; in 1879 Siena's ampelographic commission found it was Sangiovese. In the mid-19th century Clemente Santi isolated Sangiovese plantings to make a pure, long-lived wine, and his grandson Ferruccio Biondi-Santi, who had fought under [Garibaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe_Garibaldi), carried it on. In 1980 Brunello was one of the first four Italian wines to win [DOCG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denominazione_di_origine_controllata) status ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunello_di_Montalcino)).

**The wine.** Fuligni made no Riserva in 2018, so all of that juice went into this Brunello, about 35,000 bottles ([Nicks Wine Merchants](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2018-fuligni-brunello-di-montalcino)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Tuscany vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/tuscany) says producers were pleased with 2018, with volumes back to average after the small 2017; warm but not excessively hot, its watchwords were "silkiness, elegance and some surprising freshness".

**What the critics say for 2018.** As listed by [Nicks Wine Merchants](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2018-fuligni-brunello-di-montalcino):
- **[Decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decanter_%28magazine%29): 96** (Michaela Morris). It "epitomises the elegance of the vintage": pressed violet, lavender and rose with truffle and tobacco; red currant and orange, piercing acidity and chalky, magnificently textured tannins. Drink 2023 to 2034.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95** (Monica Larner, March 2023). Wild fruit, cassis, crushed stone, candied orange, rosemary and a hint of iris; silky, very well-managed tannins. Drink 2025 to 2042.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 95** (Bruce Sanderson). Pure cherry and rose hip, earth, tobacco and wild herbs; elegant and succulent. Best 2025 to 2042.
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 94**. Black cherry, hazelnut and chocolate; very perfumed, with lovely fine tannins.
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 93** (Eric Guido). Dried roses, sugar-dusted cherries and exotic spice; round, supple and velvety: "Frankly, it's hard to put this glass down."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eight years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2024 to 2039. An elegant, open-knit vintage, it is drinking beautifully now and will age. Decant an hour ahead.

**Food.** Brunello loves Tuscan food: [bistecca alla fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistecca_alla_fiorentina), wild boar stew, [pici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pici) with ragù, roast lamb, porcini, or aged [Pecorino Toscano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecorino_toscano).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Fuligni at the moment.

Sources:
- [Nicks Wine Merchants, 2018 Fuligni (critics' notes)](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2018-fuligni-brunello-di-montalcino)
- [Jancis Robinson, Tuscany vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/tuscany)
